lines: 6. THE EXTENSION RULE: the precedent's rule, restated for this commit
Rule as received: identical Lean sources outside `lean/README.md` and a
byte-identical English subject under the extraction rule, confirmed in a
fresh context and filed dated, carry this acceptance forward to a later
commit.
Accepted, with this commit as the accepted one. The rule covers exactly
what the legs of section 5 depend on: fact one fixes every path under
`lean/` except `lean/README.md`, which is the tree `gate.sh --clean`
archives (the Lean sources, `lean/Manifest.json` with its `compiler`
fields, the audit tool, the gate and self-test scripts and fixtures, the
stamp, the toolchain file, `lakefile.toml` and `lake-manifest.json` with its
Mathlib pin); fact two fixes the English statement the fidelity verdict
compared. A commit satisfying both facts has the same kernel subject and
the same English subject as the accepted one, so the kernel result, the
audit with its zero compiler axioms, the fidelity verdict and the
regeneration fact apply to it unchanged.
The Lean subject of the rule is kept as the whole `lean/` tree outside
`lean/README.md`, as the precedent stated it. The review froze its Lean
subject as the `lean/` subtree (its section 1.1) and read or censused the
whole import closure (its section 7), so the frozen-subject rule of
`docs/verification.md` binds that subtree and warrants no narrowing to the
196 closure modules; the audit, the manifest and the gate scripts that the
kernel leg relies on live outside the closure.
Operating clarifications (how the rule is applied; they change nothing in
its substance).
1. Fact one is the exit status 0 of `git diff --quiet <the checked state of
2026-09-25T03:40:15Z> <candidate> -- lean ':(exclude)lean/README.md'`.
Any difference under `lean/` other than in `lean/README.md` ends the
extension, including a change to a documentation file inside `lean/`, a
module docstring, a refusal fixture, the manifest or the audit program;
such a commit needs the legs again.
2. Fact two is byte identity, for each of the four parts, between the
extraction command's output on <path> as it stood on 2026-09-25T03:40:15Z
and on <path> at the candidate, with the four commands as recorded in
`subject_manifest.json` `extraction_rule.parts` (and to be recorded in
`native_binding.json` `english_subject`), applied unchanged with the
candidate commit in place of the accepted one, followed by the guard of
that rule on the four outputs concatenated in order at the candidate
commit, which must print nothing. A moved or renamed page, a missing
anchor, or a guard hit is a difference.
3. The confirmation is performed in a fresh context by a confirmer who is
not an author of the changes between the two commits, identified by role
and model; it names both states, the commands verbatim, their exit codes
and outputs, and its date, and is filed beside the acceptance warrant as
`delivery_confirmation_<n>.json`. It asserts no tier: the tier
assertion is this record's section 5, which the confirmation extends.
4. A nonzero exit or any byte difference means the acceptance does not
extend to that commit; the confirmer records that outcome and the
acceptance remains an acceptance of the state of 2026-09-25T03:40:15Z only.
5. The extension carries the acceptance of the Lean subject and the English
statement. It certifies nothing about text outside the English subject
(standing prose, status fields, other pages, the problem page's status),
which the integrator keeps consistent with this record under the wiki
rules.
